findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refuse cacheless completed requests**

If execution raises after `reconcile(..., status="valid")` commits but before `atomic_json(cache, ...)` completes, the `finally` block can checkpoint a valid ledger row without its result cache. After restoration, this condition does not stop that row, so execution assigns attempt 2 and sends the identical paid request again, consuming the fixed experiment budget and replacing the lost result with a duplicate; treat any prior valid row without an exact cache as recovery-required rather than redispatchable.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L38-L38](https://github.com/mporosoff/grants-scraper/blob/4e6739bdcba6bec8712df886d3566a18951a6763/AGENTS.md#L38-L38)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Block reconciled failed rows before redispatch**

When response validation fails after usage is measured and persistence is interrupted between `ledger.reconcile(..., status="failed")` and writing the `terminal` marker, the restored row has status `failed` without `terminal`. This guard excludes that state, so resuming the exact workflow sends attempt 2 for the same paid request; I reproduced this with a zero-vector response and an `OSError` during terminal persistence, after which resumption made another provider call. This is fresh evidence from the adjacent failed-reconciliation path: all reconciled cacheless rows, including `failed`, must be treated as non-redispatchable to preserve measured usage and the durable logical budget.
